title: Extended Reality in Business-to-Business Sales: Performance Implications, Adoption Drivers, and Contingency Effects
authors: Janina Mettler, Aline Lanzrath, Christian Homburg

package_source.dataset_title: Replication Data for: Extended Reality in Business-to-Business Sales: Performance Implications, Adoption Drivers, and Contingency Effects
restricted_files_not_requested: JM Dataverse Material_Extended Reality in B2B Sales.zip

eligible_reason: No DiD. The public README describes Studies 1a-1b as a 'field quasi-experiment with matched buyer-seller data' analysed by SEM (AMOS) with CFA in Stata; Studies 2a-3 are a survey and scenario experiments (SEM, MANCOVA). No panel regression with unit and time FE is listed anywhere in the package map.
design_notes: Only 'Read Me File.pdf' is public; the package zip (22 MB) is restricted and was not requested. Per the README, Study 1 data are NDA-protected company data, shared with masked or aggregated variables under an Alternative Disclosure Plan (JM-24-0534).
data_access: restricted (package zip restricted; Study 1 under Alternative Disclosure Plan, masked/aggregated)
data_provenance_note: Only the README is public. Even the restricted package carries masked/aggregated Study 1 variables.
screener_notes: Abstract flag ('quasi-experimental field data') does not correspond to a DiD; the README's study-by-method table lists SEM for Studies 1a-1b.
main_text_note: Published article checked. The text calls the company's XR rollout across selected subsidiaries a 'staggered roll-out', but Studies 1a-1b use post-rollout surveys of salespeople and customers (165 matched dyads, 220 customers), comparing XR = 1 vs XR = 0 dyads between subjects with SEM and controls. There is no pre-period, no panel, and no unit or time fixed effects, so it is not a staggered DiD design and not a near-miss.
